## K16 · K16-timer-flood-share — K16: a faster kernel entry lowers the timer-flood victim's share below its floor

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 7

Evidence: Ruled and re-ruled by the Architect (.wash/local/K20-timer-entry-billing.md, K20-rerule.md): by the pages a timer entry's kernel time is the flooder's; irq.rs bills the tail to the interrupted budget and sched::leave counts its tail as the next budget's user time, a page/code disagreement whatever the share does. K20 fixes both with a direct check in sched_oracle and a recorded negative; the share bar is not the instrument (K20's checkpoint: the finding's 445/446 was measured before B5's window; on main 31dfad3f0 the margin is 18-22 and padding raises the share). K16 no longer needs K20: rebased onto main, commits 1 and 4 pass timer-flood on both widths; seeds 4 and 5 owed.

So a flood of 1 us sleepers costs the kernel time per wakeup that is billed to no one, or not to the flooder, and a faster kernel makes the victim's share smaller, not larger. That is the test measuring something the rules do not state. Options from the implementer: (a) find where the victim's ~5% goes and bill the flooder (a kernel change, outside K16); (b) the case's tolerance revisited; (c) commit 4 keeps the old copy and waits. Your ruling: is a timer wakeup's kernel time the flooder's by budgets.md/scheduling.md as written, and if so is this a kernel finding (K20?) that K16 needs, or does the case's floor need restating against the rule? Not (b) alone, unless the rule says the share is not the flooder's to pay. K16's commit 4 holds at 277a2c060 meanwhile, and K16 waits on INIT1's merge regardless.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `7636c366e69a23792775adf69e2f1a38` · 2026-10-03T00:52:54Z

> Ruling: yes, by the pages as written a timer wakeup's kernel time is the flooder's, never the interrupted budget's. This is a kernel finding, not (b), and the case's floor stands.
> 
> Pages: timer.md "R12 for timer work" bills each expired timeout and its walk to the sleeper's budget, so a 1 us flooder "spends its own CPU share, not a neighbour's". scheduling.md "Charging" leaves only one empty walk per entry, and a device-less interrupt, to nobody.
> 
> Code: irq.rs runs expire_at_entry(), then sched::begin_billing(). From there, kernel time is cur's: the interrupted victim. On a timer-interrupt entry that is the whole tail (on_interrupt, rearm, leave's runnable() walk and reconcile). So each sleeper's wakeup charges the victim's pass, and the nobody parts come out of its wall time too. That is why padding reconcile moved the share.
> 
> New node K20 (todo, Tier A, S, no needs). Brief and exact page lines: ./.wash/local/K20-timer-entry-billing.md.
> - An entry that expired something bills the rest of its handling, its last walk included, to the budget whose item it expired last.
> - A timer entry that expired nothing is the running budget's at its slice end, and nobody's otherwise.
> - Syscall entries are unchanged.
> - A self-check pads reconcile behind a test-only feature and requires the share to move by at most 3 per thousand.
> - K20 owns time.rs expire_due's return, irq.rs's timer arm, and sched.rs's billing functions only (not runnable or reconcile, K16's).
> 
> K16 commit 4 waits for K20 to merge, then rebases. Please add K20 to K16's needs; it is a started node, so that is yours.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `9d28cf4979041537d0a9d26e2b3f2c40` · 2026-10-03T00:58:29Z

> Re-ruling: option (1). Detail: .wash/local/K20-rerule.md. It replaces the evidence and cases in K20-timer-entry-billing.md, which now points to it; the page lines stand.
> 
> Why: scheduling.md "Charging" leaves a device-less interrupt to nobody, and timer.md "R12 for timer work" says a flooder spends "its own CPU share, not a neighbour's". irq.rs bills a timer entry's tail to cur. That is a page/code disagreement, whatever the share does. Option (2) would weaken a guarantee, so it would be the owner's, and I do not recommend it.
> 
> I struck from the brief: the padding mechanism, the "about 10" negative and the "3-6 margin". The report records the non-reproduction (445/446 on ca5a6437b; 469/472 and 468/469 on 31dfad3f0) and that padding raises the share.
> 
> Added, a second leak: sched::leave sets user_since = now before runnable(), reconcile and rearm. So leave's tail is counted as the next budget's user time, which is the victim after a timer entry. The fix bills the tail's payer through to the return. leave's billing order is K20's; the bodies of runnable and reconcile stay K16's.
> 
> Proof, replacing the padding self-check (drop sched-pad; it passes with or without the defect):
> - a direct check in sched-trace/sched_oracle: every timer entry from user mode charges its time, trap to return, only to the budgets of the items it expired. The interrupted budget pays only for its own items, or at its slice end when nothing expired.
> - a recorded negative: a test-only feature keeping the old billing (like audit-billed) must fail that check on both widths. It is listed in scheduling.md's R23 diagnostic features.
> - timer-flood keeps its 450 floor, re-measured in Responsiveness, with no new bar. The other cases stay green. No model mutation.
> 
> K16: drop K20 from its needs. Agreed, it rebases and reruns timer-flood with commit 4 (both widths, seeds 3-5); if the floor holds it proceeds. Both packages edit leave(), so whichever merges second rebases.
